summary:
Turn 73 reviewed the startup-path defect's check, which the runner reproduced.

State on entry. The C11 artifact 97d6d6cc7bba4f20bdfe86f544b3c5d6 (executed as c1d2d57f…) reported violated with the oracle correspondence unreviewed; its stream shows local_address_probe with panicked true, the nil-pointer panic value, no address produced and the shared subject identity. The full-history C1 artifact also became confirmed this cycle, so the headline finding now stands on a driven proposal and commit history.

Review judgement (checker_correspondence, no_issue_found). Requirement versus predicate: the claim is that constructing a replica must not depend on reaching a fixed external probe address, and the predicate asserts panicked == false on the probe event, evaluated on the helper's own behaviour. Entry and identity: the helper is a package-level function with no inputs, and the constructor evaluates it inline as an argument to the latency table, so calling it directly exercises exactly what startup does; the probe-request prerequisite and the result share the subject identity. Oracle and the environment question, stated plainly: the source-side defect is environment-independent — the dial error is discarded and the connection dereferenced, so a failed dial becomes a nil dereference — while the observation demonstrates it in an environment of the class the claim names (no route to the probe address), so the review treats the witness as an instance of the declared applicability rather than a claim about every deployment. Limits are explicit: whether the project's own deployments reach the probe address is unknown; the check observes the helper, not a completed replica construction (which additionally needs peer addresses and a listener); and the latency table's parsing and delay arithmetic are out of scope. No counterevidence was found that the helper returns an address in this scope.

Frontier. Eleven claim families are now settled: nine confirmed violations or consequences (C1 with its six artifacts including the driven-history one, C2, C3, C4, C6, C7, C9, C10 with its three codec scenarios, C11 pending this review) and two bounded no-violation protections (C5, C8). Two candidates remain paused with resume conditions, one issue remains structurally unresolvable on a superseded artifact, and the unread items are named (the reader-side reaction to a displaced stream, whether the client caps the command size it builds, and whether any caller enables durable recording). No requirement, premise or earlier observation was weakened.
